Comedy Writing Masterclass (taught by Jerry Corley, The Joke Doctor): students build jokes using the core setup -> punchline -> tag/tag/tag structure, then add act-out tags to extend laughs from a single premise.
Students practice the underlying joke mechanic: set up an assumption then shatter it / make the audience expect one thing and deliver another, taught as the engine behind all joke formulas.

Students construct comedic premises by pairing a topic with a condition (setting, situation, or point of view) to create acute audience anticipation, then write multiple jokes from that single premise.

exercise_name: Write 15 jokes in 30 minutes / daily joke writing
description: Speed-writing practice modeled in Corley's method (e.g. writing 15 jokes in 30 minutes) and the daily-joke-writing habit Joel Byars advocates, generating volume of material to find what lands.

One of the named comedy structures taught: students write jokes by juxtaposing two things via comparison/contrast to surface incongruity (one of ~13 comedy structures in the Stand Up Comedy Clinic / Joke Doctor framework used in the masterclass).

Hot Breath! Pro members submit jokes/bits to an ongoing online writing room (Facebook group + Pro community) for peer punch-up and feedback, an accountability/feedback loop rather than a one-off lesson.

The Hot Breath! podcast format itself: 400+ interviews with working comedians extracting concrete writing/performing techniques and practice routines listeners can apply; a learning-by-listening resource rather than a guided drill.

Beginner 4-week class with live coaching and no required performance: students uncover meaningful personal narratives, develop story structure and arc, build immersive scenes with tension and stakes, and produce a working draft for ongoing development.

Highly personalized 7-week course: students develop several story ideas, shape one performance-ready personal story with a clear narrative arc, get 1:1 Zoom coaching (~30 min) and feedback on recordings between classes, and debut the finished story at a final live showcase.

Advanced 6-week workshop for graduates: students pick one story to develop and perform, strengthening narrative structure and emotional arcs, creating detailed tension-filled scenes, practicing delivery with instructor/peer feedback, rehearsing, and performing live in a student showcase.
Students record their developing story between sessions and submit it; coaches give feedback on the recording, an iterative recorded-speech-with-feedback loop used across courses.
Each student gets a private ~30-minute Zoom coaching session to refine their story's arc, scenes, and delivery with a master coach.
Students perform their developed personal story live in front of an audience at a culminating showcase, the capstone of the 101 and Performance Lab courses.

Core atomic exercise: compress any message into three connected beats - a statement of agreement (And), a contradiction/problem (But), and a consequence/call to action (Therefore) - to create a persuasive three-act narrative spine.
An ~18-minute, three-video course that walks the learner through applying the ABT framework to a sales/pitch message, effectively a guided ABT-writing drill with worked examples.
A 75-page guide (co-authored with Dr. Randy Olson) of ABT crafting exercises - drilling agreement/contradiction/consequence statements for business communications until the structure is automatic.
A longer 10-step narrative framework students map their brand/personal story onto (hero, goal, obstacle, mentor, resolution, etc.); the advanced exercise that the simpler ABT distills.

On the Business of Story podcast, Howell deconstructs speeches/ads/pitches into their ABT structure; listeners can replicate this as an analysis drill - find the And/But/Therefore in any communication.
Member is given a prompt (typically a quotation) and has up to 7 minutes to write and deliver a speech, testing quick thinking, structure under pressure, and clear delivery.
Competitor draws from prompt options (a concrete noun, abstract noun, fun fact, or quotation) and delivers a short impromptu speech with minimal prep - a fast quick-wit speaking drill.
Short, fast one-on-one debate/speech event where participants argue a spontaneous topic with almost no prep - rapid-fire impromptu argumentation, strong for quick wit.
Members debate a topic given with minimal preparation, building and rebutting arguments live - practice in thinking on your feet and persuading under time pressure.
Weekly live debates in IPDA format (designed to persuade real people, not specialists), where members take a side on a resolution and argue it conversationally - the core recurring club activity.
Member writes and delivers a polished prepared speech, then receives coaching/scoring - the structured-oratory counterpart to the spontaneous events.
Members practice extemp-style speaking (limited-prep speeches on a question) to sharpen quick thinking and organized delivery, offered alongside impromptu training.
Performance-based event where members deliver a prepared acting/interpretation piece (listed among PSDA tournament events), practicing expressive delivery and characterization.
A first-Saturday-of-the-month 2-hour live intensive where members get concentrated coaching and practice across speech and debate skills.
